pill.desc: clear, colorless to pale-yellow solution in a single-dose vial

tell: A human IgG1 kappa antibody to CTLA-4 whose concentrations reach steady state by the third dose given every 3 weeks.

clues.text: Given only by intravenous infusion after dilution. Clearance rises with body weight, which is why dosing is weight-based, and is not changed by renal or mild hepatic impairment.
Produced in Chinese hamster ovary cell culture. A sterile, preservative-free solution supplied in single-dose vials of 50 mg/10 mL or 200 mg/40 mL.
Approved under a BLA in 50 mg/10 mL and 200 mg/40 mL single-dose vials, given every 3 weeks for up to 4 doses.
No boxed warning. Fatigue, diarrhea, pruritus and rash are the most common reactions with single-agent use.
Unresectable or metastatic melanoma, adjuvant treatment of cutaneous melanoma after complete resection, and intermediate or poor-risk advanced renal cell carcinoma.
Binds CTLA-4 and blocks its interaction with CD80/CD86, which augments T-cell activation and proliferation.
The generic name begins with I and has ten letters.
